title: What could Journey become?
text: Start with the new homepage. Follow the conversation into the experience.
why: Make the new site concrete before discussing its machinery.
show: Open the homepage. Explore visit information, featured teaching, groups, and care.
decision: Which priorities should lead the homepage? This is a design sample, not a live Journey replacement.

title: Help more people find Journey.
text: The strategy, the changes, and how leadership would see the results.
why: Connect useful official pages to local discovery and accurate answers about Journey.
show: Start with the relevant strategy. Switch to Google/local results or AI answers in the dashboard.
decision: Account access is needed for real reporting. Sample performance is fictional; dated public observations are separate.

title: Make the message last all week.
text: Watch, listen, read, study, and return to the source.
why: Give existing teaching a useful home on Journey and a destination for shared clips.
show: Open the sermon player, overview and study. Then show the podcast archive and working audio.
decision: Transcript completion and connected RAG remain proposed. Confirm archive depth and source access.

title: Find the group. Meet the people.
text: Real meeting details, visible leaders, and a calendar people can use.
why: Help people decide whether a group fits and understand how to join.
show: Explore the directory and calendar, then Patrick’s Friday 6–7 AM men’s study in the Journey lobby.
decision: Patrick’s details were supplied for the comp. Confirm the full group roster and available signup connections.

title: An email becomes a prepared update.
text: Show exactly what an agent prepares and what a human approves.
why: Reduce copying and checking while keeping Journey in control of public information.
show: Review Patrick’s sample email next to the proposed changes; approve it and show the attendance charts update.
decision: No real inbox or accounts are connected. Agree authorized senders, reviewers and publishing permissions.

title: The right people. A covered Sunday.
text: Move from the coordinator’s board to the volunteer’s phone.
why: Make open positions, confirmations and backups visible; make responding easy.
show: Drag a volunteer into a position, then open the phone sample. Accept, decline, or type a question.
decision: Fictional volunteers; replies stay in the separate demo. Confirm whether production connects to their existing scheduler.

title: Know what is connecting.
text: Participation, content, questions, and the details behind the charts.
why: Help leadership spot useful patterns, reporting gaps and decisions needing attention.
show: Open an attendance trend, missing reports, or channel results based on what they ask. Use the brief for a concise summary.
decision: Private performance and attendance are illustrative. Real public facts are labeled. Headcounts do not establish individual retention.

title: What would it take to build?
text: The website, connections, launch scope, and decisions still to make.
why: Turn interest in the examples into a concrete discussion of the production build.
show: Open scope when asked. Connect the selected capabilities to the required access, content and implementation.
decision: No fixed price or launch date is established. The reading library is optional; verify integration access before promising automatic imports.

title: A library worth exploring.
text: A curated reading shelf using the supplied book list and cover art.
why: Illustrate a possible reading resource for the Journey community.
show: Browse covers and individual books. This is separate from the core website scope.
decision: Optional only. No affiliate program is included. Links go to individual books, not the original wishlist.

title: Make the invitation something people feel.
text: Kingdom Conference: a visual event page and the finished social ad.
why: Use the familiar conference as an example of stronger event marketing within the broader site proposal.
show: Show guests, inline music video and the day-by-day schedule. Play the conference ad from the proposal’s sample section.
decision: The event page and ad are comps. Past speaker videos do not promise conference topics. Keep this as the final example, not the opening pitch.
